clue.text: Doctor dictates crucial experimental procedure

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician lays down the vital procedure for an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is a verb telling you to rework 'dictates'.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test was originally a chemical assay for gold, now any decisive trial of worth.

clue.text: Like much work in office of the ministry

definitions.meaning: first sense: concerned with clerks and paperwork
second sense: relating to the clergy

explanation.walkthrough: 'ministry' suggests a government department, which fits the office; it means the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes routine desk paperwork and also anything belonging to clergymen.

clue.text: Vehicle in which one can take flight

definitions.text: Vehicle in which one can take flight

parts.words: Vehicle in which one can take flight
parts.note: taking a flight sounds like flying, but on a two-level bus you climb a flight of stairs

explanation.walkthrough: 'take flight' suggests an aircraft or an escape; it means a flight of stairs between the decks of a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus with two passenger levels connected by a staircase, typical of London.

clue.text: Authority to apply pressure internally

indicators.note: the pressure goes on the inside of the other word

parts.note: to exert force is to apply it
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Officialdom deciding to lean on someone from within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Authority' reads as a power, but it is the person who knows the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: An authority on a subject is a specialist whose knowledge is trusted.

clue.text: Tense, as pupil is in audition

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the word is spoken out loud

parts.note: a pupil is taught

explanation.surface: A nervous pupil at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' suggests a tryout, but here it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means stretched tight, and so strained or nervous.

clue.text: Finest example to which nothing can be added

definitions.meaning: first sense: the most up-to-date, best model

definitions.text: to which nothing can be added
definitions.meaning: second sense: the final remark that closes an argument

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description, but it splits after 'example' into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the ultimate in fashion or quality and the closing remark that settles a debate.

clue.text: Fruit one can't take off

definitions.meaning: first sense: the green-fleshed fruit with furry skin
second sense: the flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' suggests removing a peel; it means getting airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a fuzzy-skinned fruit and to a New Zealand bird unable to fly.

clue.text: Supposed I oppose editor

parts.note: 'I'm agin' is a dialect way of saying I'm against

explanation.surface: Someone thinking they ought to stand up to their editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agin' is a dialect or jocular form of against.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed and imagined both mean thought or assumed, perhaps without good reason.

clue.text: Scary attitude in hospital — arm is mistreated

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the following words, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: A frightening outlook spreads on a ward where a patient's arm has been badly handled.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'hospital' through 'arm is' to the first letter of 'mistreated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmism is the habit of raising needless fears, an outlook that scares people.

clue.text: Fellows with university providing courses in writing

parts.note: fellows are men

explanation.surface: Academics, together with their university, supply a written programme of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests academic study, but they are the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is the written list of dishes or courses offered at a meal.

clue.text: Inspiring? Awesome!

definitions.meaning: first sense, read literally: drawing in air, taking a breath

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' is read literally as breathing in, which the answer also describes word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stunning leaves you gasping; and inhaling is literally the act of drawing air into the lungs.

clue.text: Thief finally struck wildly at policeman

indicators.note: take only the end letter of the word before

parts.note: last letter K

indicators.note: the following letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal lashing out at an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives the K ending 'struck', and 'wildly' rearranges AT POLICEMAN to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kleptomaniac has a compulsion to steal, so is a thief, though not for gain.

clue.text: Lid of bottle sailors kept in bar

indicators.note: the sailors are held within the bar, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to bar is to stop
a ship's sailors are its crew

explanation.surface: Seamen drinking in a pub, with a bottle's cap the only detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but here it is the verb meaning to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-top is a cap that twists onto a threaded bottle neck to seal it.

clue.text: See 16 across
From Baltimore go North, in area near Washington

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the next words

explanation.surface: Travel directions: leave Baltimore and head north to somewhere close to Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington here is the state in the Pacific Northwest, not the capital near Baltimore.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is the US state lying directly south of Washington State.

clue.text: TV programme crew is going to show

definitions.meaning: first sense: a long-running BBC children's television show
second sense: the flag a ship's crew hoists to signal it is about to sail

explanation.walkthrough: The blue peter is a blue flag with a white square, flown in harbour when a vessel is about to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's show took its name from the naval signal flag, raised before a ship's departure.

clue.text: Marine crustacean exposed, retaining salt

indicators.note: the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: bare means exposed
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: A sea creature left bare and crusted with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt here is sodium chloride, written NaCl in chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnacles are crustaceans that cling to rocks and the hulls of ships.

clue.text: Took out old hat

definitions.meaning: first sense: went out on a date with someone
second sense: old-fashioned, out of date

explanation.walkthrough: 'Took out old hat' reads as removing a hat; it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Courting someone means taking them on dates; and outmoded things are described as no longer current.

clue.text: Energy put into compelling drawing

indicators.note: the energy is placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: driving means forceful, compelling
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Effort invested in a powerful sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' looks like a picture, but it is the verb, as in drawing a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Deriving means obtaining something from a source, as drawing does in 'drawing strength from'.

clue.text: How grade might be lowered for nasty person

parts.note: the clue asks how a grade is cut; the reply begins with 'to', the direction of the cut
the reply goes on with the article 'a' before the new letter grade
a mark lowered ends at the poor letter grade D

explanation.surface: A teacher dropping a mark as a punishment for an unpleasant pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a loose, whole-phrase reading rather than strict pieces: answer the question 'how might a grade be lowered?' with three words, TO A D.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a toad means they are loathsome or contemptible.

clue.text: Display, so to speak, a kind of horse or cow

indicators.note: the word for display is said out loud, giving a same-sounding spelling

parts.note: to air something is to display it
a Shire is a heavy draught horse breed

explanation.surface: Showing off a breed of farm animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse or cow' suggests one answer for both; the horse is wordplay and the cow is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ayrshire is a Scottish breed of dairy cattle from the county of Ayr.

clue.text: Resentment voiced in private

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word for resentment sounds like the answer

parts.note: rancour is bitter resentment

explanation.surface: Bitterness expressed behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a soldier of the lowest rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranker is a soldier in the ranks, such as a private, rather than an officer.

clue.text: Herb contrary gardener put with flower

parts.note: a rose is a flower
the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary, how does your garden grow?'

explanation.surface: An awkward gardener planting a herb beside a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' looks like a description, but with 'gardener' it points to the nursery-rhyme Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic shrub whose leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: Guy paying court with diamonds, say, and gold

parts.note: diamonds are an example of a suit in cards
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A man wooing a lady with jewels and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' looks like jewels for a sweetheart, but it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man wooing a woman, hoping to marry her.

clue.text: Plane, for example, flying above Britain

indicators.note: letters flying about are scattered and land in a new order

explanation.surface: An aircraft soaring over the British Isles.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane seems to be an aircraft in flight, but the word itself is the example: a clipped form of aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Plane is a shortened form of aeroplane, so it is an instance of a shortened word.

clue.text: Be inclined, in turn, to store money

definitions.meaning: first sense: to tilt sideways while turning, as an aircraft does

explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' looks like 'in sequence', but it means while turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft and cyclists lean into a curve; the same word means depositing savings with a financial institution.

clue.text: Side winds

definitions.meaning: second sense: breezes or light winds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Side winds' reads as crosswinds; 'side' is the British slang for swagger or pretension.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected superiority is called 'putting on airs', and gentle breezes are also called airs.

clue.text: Is repeatedly put in academic stream

indicators.note: the word is said more than once, so it is written out twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A short phrase placed into a scholarly river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames at Oxford, a university city, is known locally by this name, hence a scholarly river.

clue.text: British citizen, fellow taken in by recluse

indicators.note: the fellow is housed within the recluse, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a loner is a recluse
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A hermit offering shelter to a man from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' looks like any man, but here it is a college fellow, a don.
explanation.definitionFit: A Londoner is a resident of the British capital, so a British citizen of a particular city.

clue.text: Afflicted, become ill without treatment recommended initially

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the illness surrounds the initials

parts.note: to sicken is to become ill

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: first letter T
first letter R

explanation.surface: Struck down by illness because no recommended treatment was given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but it is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricken means badly affected by disease or trouble, as in grief-stricken.
